metadata.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations (Chen, Kornblith, Norouzi, Hinton, 2020)
metadata.framework: contrastive learning with large batch in-batch negatives and strong augmentations
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:2002.05709.

nodes.name: Data augmentation pipeline
nodes.statement: For each image $\mathbf{x}$, draw two random augmentations $t, t' \sim \mathcal{T}$ producing a positive pair $(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_i, \tilde{\mathbf{x}}_j)$. The augmentation family $\mathcal{T}$ includes random cropping + resize, color distortion (jitter, grayscale), and Gaussian blur. Strong augmentations are critical: the composition of random crop + color distortion is found to be the most important.

nodes.name: Encoder and projection head
nodes.statement: An encoder $f(\cdot)$ (e.g., ResNet-50) maps augmented images to representations: $\mathbf{h}_i = f(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_i)$. A projection head $g(\cdot)$ (MLP with one hidden layer + ReLU) maps to a lower-dimensional space: $\mathbf{z}_i = g(\mathbf{h}_i) = W^{(2)} \sigma(W^{(1)} \mathbf{h}_i)$. The contrastive loss is computed on $\mathbf{z}_i$; the representation $\mathbf{h}_i$ is used for downstream tasks.

nodes.name: NT-Xent loss (normalized temperature-scaled cross entropy)
nodes.statement: For a mini-batch of $N$ images yielding $2N$ augmented examples, the loss for positive pair $(i,j)$: $\ell_{i,j} = -\log \frac{\exp(\mathrm{sim}(\mathbf{z}_i, \mathbf{z}_j) / \tau)}{\sum_{k=1}^{2N} \mathbb{1}_{[k \ne i]} \exp(\mathrm{sim}(\mathbf{z}_i, \mathbf{z}_k) / \tau)}$ where $\mathrm{sim}(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}) = \mathbf{u}^\top \mathbf{v} / (\|\mathbf{u}\| \|\mathbf{v}\|)$ is cosine similarity and $\tau$ is temperature. The full loss averages over all $2N$ positive pairs. Each example uses the other $2(N-1)$ examples as negatives.

nodes.name: Large batch training
nodes.statement: SimCLR uses large mini-batches ($N$ up to 8192, yielding $2N = 16384$ examples) to provide enough in-batch negatives. Trained with LARS optimizer for stability at large batch sizes. No memory bank or queue is needed; all negatives come from the current batch.

nodes.name: SimCLR algorithm
nodes.statement: SimCLR training: (1) Sample mini-batch of $N$ images. (2) Apply two random augmentations to each, getting $2N$ views. (3) Encode all views through $f$ and $g$. (4) Compute NT-Xent loss over all $2N(2N-1)$ pairs. (5) Update $f$ and $g$ by SGD/LARS. No momentum encoder, no queue, no memory bank.

nodes.name: Importance of augmentation composition
nodes.statement: Systematic ablation shows that no single augmentation suffices; the composition of random crop and color distortion is essential. Random crop alone creates a shortcut (color histogram discrimination); adding color distortion forces learning of more semantic features. This finding is SimCLR's key design insight.
conclusions: Composition of random crop + color distortion is critical
Removing color distortion drops linear eval accuracy by ~10%
Augmentation design is more important than architectural choices

nodes.name: Projection head and representation quality
nodes.statement: The nonlinear projection head $g$ significantly improves representation quality: linear evaluation on $\mathbf{h}$ (before projection) improves by ~10% compared to using $\mathbf{z}$ (after projection) or using $\mathbf{h}$ without a projection head. The projection head removes information useful for the contrastive task (e.g., color) but not for downstream tasks.
conclusions: Nonlinear projection head improves downstream representation quality
Information loss in projection is beneficial (removes task-specific shortcuts)
Evaluate representations BEFORE the projection head

nodes.name: ImageNet linear evaluation results
nodes.statement: SimCLR with ResNet-50 (4x width) achieves 76.5% top-1 linear evaluation accuracy on ImageNet, approaching supervised ResNet-50 (76.5%). With larger ResNets, SimCLR matches or exceeds supervised baselines. Semi-supervised results: 1% labels achieves 75.5% with fine-tuning.
